main_body: A bare, snow-dusted birch-like tree: a tall pale trunk with a branching bare crown and a small snow patch at the base.
top_band: none: the column through the trunk shows pale trunk tone (L=206) with dark bark marks from row 12 down, and no horizontal top surface. The crown is a sparse branch tangle.
evidence: The object is an organic tree with a thin vertical trunk and a branching crown. It has no horizontal top surface or flat front face to measure, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract barely applies. The column scan shows only trunk tone with dark bark flecks, and the crown is a see-through branch tangle with no mass reading as a canopy top. The trunk is a plain vertical cylinder with no cap or rim. Strictly, no top band is visible and the drawing reads as a flat vertical silhouette. When in doubt, fail.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 9 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. All of its dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), so the outline is neutral near-black rather than a tinted material tone. The trunk is a narrow pale grey strip with a few dark flecks and only about 3 lightness steps. The crown is a sparse scatter of dark grey pixels with a few white snow dots. Next to the lush, multi-green, richly shaded references, it looks much thinner and more sticker-like. The 0% flat-fill coverage only reflects the narrow, sparse shapes and does not show richness.
